title: Lady A’s Charles Kelley Shares Blood Cancer Diagnosis: ‘I’m Confident That We’re Going to Get Through It’
description: Charles Kelley, the co-lead vocalist and founding member of the country band Lady A, has been diagnosed with the rare blood cancer multiple myeloma.
body:
Charles Kelley, the co-lead vocalist and founding member of the country band Lady A, has been diagnosed with the rare blood cancer multiple myeloma. 

	The singer shared the news on his Instagram on Tuesday, with the caption “A little health update” under the video.

	“Hey everybody. Just wanted to give a quick update on some health issues I’m dealing with,” Kelley said. “I had [a] couple random rib fractures that happened, which sparked my doctor into having me do several different blood tests. And one of the last blood tests we did, they found a blood cancer in there called multiple myeloma, and it’s rare.”
	

	“I’m young, I feel healthy, and the treatments I will say have just come so far, even in the past five years,” he continued. “Even life expectancy just far exceeds what it used to be and, I don’t know, I feel really hopeful. I really do.”


	Kelley likened sharing the news of his health with his sobriety journey: “Just getting this stuff off your chest is so freeing, and it takes the power away from it a little bit that we want to let y’all know what was going on. But we’re going to get through it. You know, I think in sobriety it’s all about one day at a time and that we’re not in control, and so that’s the way we’re looking at it.”

	Kelley has been outspoken about his struggles with alcohol, and in 2022, the band — formerly known as Lady Antebellum — shared that they would be postponing the remainder of their “Request Line Tour” in support of Charles Kelley’s “journey to sobriety.”

	The singer concluded the video by sharing that he is “hopeful” and will “try” to let fans in throughout the journey. “It’s just another hurdle, and you know, I’m confident that we’re going to get through it.”
	

	From Dec. 10 through 21, the group will perform a run of Christmas shows as part of the “This Winter’s Night” tour.

schema.headline: Lady A’s Charles Kelley Shares Blood Cancer Diagnosis: ‘I’m Confident That We’re Going to Get Through It’

title: Casey Bloys Poised to Run HBO and Paramount+ as Cindy Holland Confirms Her Exit From Studio on Eve of Merger Closing
description: HBO chief Casey Bloys is poised to take the reins of all of Paramount and Warner Bros. streaming operations once the two companies merge. On Tuesday
body:
HBO chief Casey Bloys is poised to take the reins of all of Paramount and Warner Bros. streaming operations once the two companies merge. On Tuesday, Cindy Holland announced she was stepping down from her role running Paramount+ and other direct to consumer streamers under the Paramount umbrella.

	The shuffle comes as Paramount Skydance is days away from closing its hard-won $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery.


	Holland confirmed her departure in a memo to staff sent Tuesday afternoon, acknowledging that Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison has made the decision regarding streaming leadership, although she did not reference Bloys by name.
	

	“As David readies for the next phase of his vision, we’ve discussed my role and the future of the combined businesses. David is optimizing for HBO stability as we move into this next chapter, and I fully support that. I know this team has the leadership and expertise to manage through the transition and the next phase of the company, and to this end today will mark my last day here,” Holland wrote.

	Over the past few weeks, speculation emerged that Bloys was likely to come over post merger in the top role overseeing all streaming operations. Bloys is a near 25-year veteran of HBO who has steered TV’s most prestigious brand through choppy waters and three massive corporate takeovers in eight years. There’s also speculation that JB Perrette, who now heads streaming business operations and gaming for WBD, will join Bloys in steering HBO, HBO Max and Paramount+. 

	Holland was part of the pioneering team that built Netflix into the world’s biggest subscription streaming platform. Her 18-year run at that streamer included nine years as Vice President of Original Content. Holland established the network’s original programming strategy and oversaw the teams behind flagship hits like “House of Cards,” “Stranger Things,” “The Crown,” “Icarus,” “When They See Us” and “The Queen’s Gambit.” Between Netflix and Paramount, Holland served as CEO of Sister — the production company formed by Elizabeth Murdoch. Her exit comes as the industry speculates wildly about the fate of other division leaders across both companies.
	

	Here is Holland’s full memo:

	When I joined David’s team in January 2025, we proceeded to set three goals: i) advise on the Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition, ii) integrate and transform Paramount+ & revive Pluto TV, and iii) build an unparalleled team in this industry. In just over 12 months, I’m proud to say we accomplished all three and it’s been a joy to work closely with all of you.

	Together with the Product team, we drove significant strategic and organizational change across DTC — building a new foundation for growth on both services, while investing in greater depth and breadth of programming and delivering strong revenue, profit, and subscriber growth for the division.

	As David readies for the next phase of his vision, we’ve discussed my role and the future of the combined businesses. David is optimizing for HBO stability as we move into this next chapter, and I fully support that. I know this team has the leadership and expertise to manage through the transition and the next phase of the company, and to this end today will mark my last day here.

	As I reflect on my time here and all that we’ve built together in this short time, what stands out most to me is this team. I have never been more proud of a group of people. What we’ve accomplished together is remarkable — landing quarter after quarter while navigating extraordinary uncertainty and change with resilience, focus and ambition. We grew Paramount+ to an all-time subscriber high, delivered the best retention in the service’s history, and drove double-digit growth in both engagement and revenue. We built an extraordinary content pipeline, greenlighting more than 40 new and returning series and setting all-time records with Landman, the most-watched series in Paramount+ history, and Dutton Ranch, the service’s biggest original series debut ever. We transformed live sports into a powerful streaming growth engine, securing landmark agreements with UFC and Zuffa Boxing and expanding our WNBA and UEFA Champions League rights – with UFC Freedom 250 becoming the largest-ever audience for an exclusive live event on Paramount+ and UFC 329 setting a new platform record for peak concurrent streams for an exclusive live event. And we undertook Pluto TV’s biggest product transformation in a decade, dramatically increasing registered viewing and VOD consumption while delivering strong financial performance across the business. These are extraordinary accomplishments – but what makes me proudest is how we achieved them: together, with an unwavering commitment to our audiences, our creative partners and one another.
	

	I joined Paramount because I believe in these businesses, and because I believe wholeheartedly that the combination of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery serves the best interests of artists and audiences worldwide. I’m looking forward to seeing what you all accomplish together in this next, momentous chapter.

schema.headline: Casey Bloys Poised to Run HBO and Paramount+ as Cindy Holland Confirms Her Exit From Studio on Eve of Merger Closing

title: Penn Badgley Swore Off Sex Scenes. His Wife Says It Was Not Her Idea: ‘He Decided to Do This for Mental Health Reasons’
description: Penn Badgley infamously swore off sex scenes before the production of “You” Season 4, revealing on a viral episode of his “Podcrushed” podcast in Fe
body:
Penn Badgley infamously swore off sex scenes before the production of “You” Season 4, revealing on a viral episode of his “Podcrushed” podcast in Feb. 2013 that he told showrunner Sera Gamble he was no longer interested in filming intimate scenes on camera. The actor then told Variety later that same month that “it’s important to me in my real life to not have” sex scenes, clarifying: “My fidelity in my relationship. It’s important to me.”
	

	Cut to more than three years later and Badgley’s wife, Domino Kirke-Badgley, is speaking out after spending all this time being accused online of blocking her husband from doing sex scenes. When Badgley cited his marriage as a reason he did not want to act in sex scenes anymore, social media was quick to come for Kirke-Badgley, even though Penn had cited her as the reason he even accepted the lusty lead role in “You” in the first place.


	“A few years ago, the internet decided I’d asked my husband to stop doing sex scenes. The truth is, my husband decided to do this for mental health reasons,” Kirke-Badgley wrote on Instagram. “After working in the industry since he was just 12 years old, believe me, it was time. In the entertainment world, they call actors ‘puppets’ behind their backs, and it’s even more disturbing when they start out as child actors… after years of trying, Penn decided to take a stand and let the world see him. And guess what, he hasn’t lost fans and he’s still getting hired!”

	“The characters that my husband has played over the years, people have come to expect that he will continue to play that guy,” she added in the video post. “I was super happy for him and very proud of him because I understood how major it was, and yeah … it’s just relational hygiene.”
	

	Badgley has been married since 2017 to Kirke-Badgley, who “encouraged” him to play Joe on “You” even though the part required him to film various sex scenes.

	“There’s almost nothing I could say with more consecration. That aspect of Hollywood has always been very disturbing to me — and that aspect of the job, that mercurial boundary — has always been something that I actually don’t want to play with at all,” Badgely told Variety in 2023. “I told [Sara Gamble before Season 4] kind of my desire, and she immediately was accepting and responsive. I’m always very practical. I said I know it can’t be none, because there’s something coded into the DNA of the show, and I signed the contract, and so it is what it is but as little as possible would be my preference.”

	There were fewer sex scenes in “You” Season 4, and all of them were performed fully clothed as a result of Badgley speaking up. The actor’s initial comments earned a polarizing response online, with his detractors criticizing him for equating sex scenes with real sex. Many of Badgley’s critics pointed out that intimacy coordinators are now a staple in Hollywood so that sex scenes remain safe during filming. He later told GQ magazine that his comments got “blown out of proportion.”

	“What I was speaking about wasn’t actually the final product,” Badgley said. “It was sort of like the culture inherent to the production of all movies, but particularly those scenes. It’s like, look, we know that Hollywood has had a history of flagrant exploitation and abuse.”

	Badgley said he was “nervous to even have that conversation” with “You” showrunner Sera Gamble, adding, “It was not easy. It was easy because of Sera’s response, and I felt relieved. But technically speaking, if I thought I’d had the ability to set that boundary earlier, I would have. We shall see if setting that boundary, of course, has any ramifications. Just simply, it does limit the number of projects you can be a part of.”

	Next up for Badgley is the romantic comedy “You Deserve Each Other,” co-starring Meghann Fahy.

schema.headline: Penn Badgley Swore Off Sex Scenes. His Wife Says It Was Not Her Idea: ‘He Decided to Do This for Mental Health Reasons’

title: Ex-‘American Idol’ Contestant Caleb Flynn Found Guilty of Murdering Wife
description: Caleb Flynn, a former contestant on “American Idol,” was found guilty of murdering his wife in their Ohio home. A jury deliberated for around two ho
body:
Caleb Flynn, a former contestant on “American Idol,” was found guilty of murdering his wife in their Ohio home. A jury deliberated for around two hours on Tuesday and convicted him on all nine counts that he faced of of murder, assault and tampering with evidence.

	On the morning of Monday, Feb. 16, Ashley Flynn, 37, was found dead in the couple’s Ohio home in Tipp City. Caleb, 40, called 911 around 2:30 a.m. and said that someone had broken into their home and shot Ashley, who was pronounced dead at the scene. According to local outlets, Caleb told police that he didn’t see anybody in the home, but his garage door was open. Police reportedly found a side door to the garage that was open and that there was fridge in front of the door that would’ve needed to be pushed to open it. Caleb was booked into the Miami County Jail on the following Thursday.
	

	“While the defendant told law enforcement that he was sleeping, his electronic devices documented something different. They documented movement and activity in the hours leading up to Ashley’s murder,” said Matthew C. Joseph, assistant prosecuting attorney for the Miami County Prosecuting Attorney’s Office said in his closing argument. “The defendant said he was sleeping. His devices say he was awake and moving.”


	The attorney added, “Being the victim allowed him to do that without being the husband who left his wife for a mistress. Instead, he’d be the husband whose wife was tragically murdered by an unknown intruder.”

	Caleb was a contestant on “American Idol” in 2013. In 2013, he said in his “Road to Hollywood” interview on “American Idol” that he was a music pastor and that his wife encouraged him to audition for the singing competition show. “I absolutely love the lord and I love my wife more than anything,” he said in his interview. “She is very, very pretty. I love her. I’m just a normal person who absolutely loves to sing more than anything in the world.”

schema.headline: Ex-‘American Idol’ Contestant Caleb Flynn Found Guilty of Murdering Wife

title: Ringo Starr, David Byrne, Joan Baez Donate Unqiue Items for Housing Works Auction
description: Ringo Starr, David Byrne, Joan Baez, and more have donated items to be auction in Housing Works’ second annual Turn It Up! auction, which is open th
body:
Ringo Starr, David Byrne, Joan Baez, and more have donated items to be auction in Housing Works’ second annual Turn It Up! auction, which is open through Oct. 1.

	The National frontman Matt Berninger, Ani DiFranco, Richard Hell, Def Leppard’s Rick Allen, photographer Bob Gruen and others have donated items as well.

	Items include a T-shirt autographed by Starr, original artworks by Byrne and Baez, a signed drum head from Rick Allen, and a color print of Gruen’s iconic photo of John Lennon standing in front of the Statue of Liberty — see all the items and bid here. 
	

	Founded in 1990 by people living with HIV/AIDS and their allies, Housing Works emerged during the AIDS crisis in response to the urgent need for housing, healthcare, and support for people living with HIV/AIDS. Over the decades, the New York City nonprofit has expanded its work to address housing instability, homelessness, healthcare access, HIV/AIDS, and social justice.


	Housing Works provides direct services including housing, healthcare, behavioral health care, and supportive services, while also advocating for policy changes affecting New Yorkers experiencing homelessness, poverty, healthcare barriers, and housing instability.

	The organization’s work remains connected to New York City, where it operates programs and services while advocating for communities that have historically faced significant barriers to housing and healthcare.

	Turn It Up! is open for bidding through October 1, 2026.

	Of the Lennon photo, the entry reads: “The US government was trying to deport John Lennon because of his support for the peace movement during the Vietnam war so I suggested we take a picture at the Statue of Liberty to illustrate that America was supposed to welcome people. Since Lennon’s death, this photo has taken on a new meaning as people think of John Lennon in terms of personal freedom similar to the Statue of Liberty.”
	

	Connect with Housing Works: Website

title: Jennifer Lawrence to Star in Zach Cregger’s ‘The Flood’
description: Jennifer Lawrence will star in Zach Cregger‘s buzzy sci-fi thriller “The Flood” from Warner Bros. and New Line Cinema. Cregger is set to write, prod
body:
Jennifer Lawrence will star in Zach Cregger‘s buzzy sci-fi thriller “The Flood” from Warner Bros. and New Line Cinema. Cregger is set to write, produce and direct the film, which is set for release on Aug. 11, 2028. 

	Amblin Entertainment serves as producer alongside Roy Lee and Miri Yoon of Vertigo Entertainment. Plot details and further casting remain under wraps. 

	Lawrence, an Academy Award winner for 2012’s “Silver Linings Playbook,” brings some serious prestige to Cregger’s latest genre play. Probably best known for her breakout as the face of “The Hunger Games” franchise, Lawrence’s most recent film credits are “Die My Love” with Robert Pattinson, Gene Stupnitsky’s rom-com “No Hard Feelings” and the A24 drama “Causeway.” One of her other upcoming projects includes the Martin Scorsese thriller “What Happens at Night.” She will also appear in the upcoming “Hunger Games” prequel “Sunrise on the Reaping.” 
	

	“The Flood” sees Cregger reunite with Warner Bros. after the studio released his twisty 2025 horror mystery “Weapons.” A follow-up to his 2022 breakout “Barbarian,” the film was a commercial and critical success, grossing $270 million worldwide off a budget of less than $40 million. The film also earned Amy Madigan a Best Supporting Actress Oscar for her role as the evil Aunt Gladys, who, in the film, steals a classroom full of children in the middle of the night right under the noses of their manic teacher and overprotective parents. 


	“Mike, Pam and the whole Warner Bros./New Line team were an absolute dream to collaborate with on ‘Weapons,’ and I couldn’t be happier to dive in with them again. Jennifer is one of a kind, and I’m beyond excited to see her in this role,” Cregger said.
	

	Warner Bros. co-chairs Mike De Luca and Pam Abdy added, “Jennifer Lawrence is one of the most gifted and compelling actors working today, and we are thrilled to have her at the center of Zach’s bold and wholly original vision for ‘The Flood.’ Following our extraordinary experience together on ‘Weapons,’ we could not be more excited to reunite with Zach and the team at Vertigo, as well as Amblin to bring this ambitious film to audiences around the world.”

	Lawrence is represented by LBI Entertainment and Hansen, Jacobson, Teller, Hoberman, Newman, Warren, Richman, Rush, Kaller & Gellman.

schema.headline: Jennifer Lawrence to Star in Zach Cregger’s ‘The Flood’

body:

	Amazon‘s Prime Big Deal Days (a.k.a. “Fall Prime Day) is back for another season of savings, with 48 hours of Prime member-exclusive deals ahead of the holidays.

	This year’s Prime Big Deal Days run from October 6 to 7, with millions of deals across 35 categories, according to Amazon. Prime members will get first dibs on the discounts, with fast, free shipping to have all the items delivered to their door.


	Not a Prime member? Get a 30-day free trial here to shop Prime Big Deal Days and take advantage of all the other Amazon Prime member perks, like free TV shows and movies on Prime Video, free music streaming on Amazon Music and more.


	Here’s what else you need to know about Amazon Prime Big Deal Days 2026.

	As mentioned earlier, this year’s Amazon Prime Big Deal Days takes place over two days: October 6 and 7. The deals kick off on October 6 at 12:01 a.m. PT, though some early deals are already live on the site.
	
		What Brands Are on Sale for Prime Big Deal Days 2026?	

	As always, the biggest discounts will be on Amazon devices, which now include everything from Fire TV Sticks and Fire TVs, to Ring cameras, Echo smart speakers, HD tablets, Kindle e-readers and more. Amazon’s Fire TV 4K Streaming Stick, for example, is already marked down by 64% off here.

	Other brands on sale for Prime Big Deal Days include Barefoot Dreams, FAO Schwarz, NEST New York, Princess Polly, Shark, Soundcore by Anker and UGG, per Amazon. A quick search of the site also turns up deals on top-rated products from Bissell, Breville, Hisense, iRobot, KitchenAid, Samsung and TCL, among others.


	Amazon says new deal drops will take place three times a day: at midnight (PT), 8 a.m. and 1 p.m. The deals will be labeled as “Today’s Big Deals,” and are all limited-time offers that will expire as soon as the items are sold out.
	
		Do You Have to Be a Prime Member to Shop Amazon Big Deal Days?	

	Amazon has thousands of daily deals that are available to shop without needing a Prime membership, but the best discounts and offers will be reserved for Prime members. Make sure you’re logged into your Prime account before you start shopping as that is how you’ll see the cheapest or latest discounted price.

	Prime members can also get items delivered in as fast as 30 minutes with regular delivery vehicles or through Prime Air drone delivery, which is currently available in select cities across Arizona, Florida, Kansas, Louisiana, Michigan, Nebraska and Texas.

	Millions of items are also available for free same-day or next-day delivery for Prime members in more than 10,000 cities and towns across the country.
	
		Best Prime Membership Deals 2026: Get Free Trial	

	A Prime membership costs $14.99/month but you can test drive the service with a 30-day free trial here.

	After that, your best bet is to sign up for an annual plan, which saves you 23% off versus paying month to month.

	College students and young adults ages 18-24, meantime, can save 50% off an Amazon Prime membership. Plus, get 5% cashback on select items across beauty, fashion, electronics and other categories online.

	This is the fourth annual Prime Big Deal Days event. Originally launched in 2022 as the “Prime Early Access Sale,” the name was changed in 2023 to “Prime Big Deal Days.” The event was created as a fall shopping event for Amazon and a counterpart to Prime Day in the summer.

title: ‘The Little Prince’ Live-Action Movie Set With ‘The Imitation Game’ Director Morten Tyldum and Simon Beaufoy (EXCLUSIVE)
description: “The Little Prince” is getting a new big-screen treatment with “The Imitation Game” director Morten Tyldum set to helm an ambitious live-action feat
body:
“The Little Prince” is getting a new big-screen treatment with “The Imitation Game” director Morten Tyldum set to helm an ambitious live-action feature inspired by the life of French aviator Antoine de Saint-Exupéry. 

	Simon Beaufoy, the Oscar-winning screenwriter of “Slumdog Millionaire,” is writing the script for the film which is being developed with Le Petit Prince Groupe, guardian of the Saint-Exupéry estate. 


	The big-scale family adventure project hails from Aton Soumache, the well-known French producer behind Mark Osborne’s 2015 animated feature “The Little Prince.” The latter world premiered at Cannes and grossed close to $100 million worldwide, as well as won the César for best animated film and the BAFTA Children’s Award for best feature film.
	

	This new project will pull elements from French comic book artist and filmmaker Joann Sfar’s acclaimed graphic adaptation of “The Little Prince,” portraying the bond between the Little Prince and the Aviator. 

	The film will blend Saint-Exupéry’s real-life story as a pioneering aviator and writer with the fantastical world of “The Little Prince.” Saint-Exupéry’s story will unfold in live action, while the Little Prince will be created using visual effects. 

	“I see it as a very cinematic and epic story, one that gives us a wonderful opportunity to ask big questions,” Tyldum said. “This is a story about love, grief and loss. It’s about hope, following your heart’s desire and seeing life as a big adventure.”

	First published in 1943, “The Little Prince” has sold more than 200 million copies worldwide and has been translated into some 600 languages and dialects.
	

	Beaufoy, whose credits also include “The Full Monty” and “The Hunger Games: Catching Fire,” described adapting the book as both daunting and exhilarating. 

	“‘The Little Prince’ is the most extraordinary text because it never goes out of fashion. It talks to the child in every human being,” Beaufoy said. “Everybody relates to that small child, who is the voice of truth that you sometimes don’t even want to hear.” He added that turning such a revered work into a broader cinematic canvas was “a thrilling responsibility.”

	Sfar, who worked with the Saint-Exupéry family on his graphic adaptation roughly 15 years ago, said the new film grew out of that longstanding relationship.

	“I am grateful for the trust placed in me by the Saint Exupéry family, alongside whom I created ‘The Little Prince’ comic book 15 years ago, to develop the concept of this unique film,” Sfar said. “With Simon Beaufoy writing it and Morten Tyldum directing it, I couldn’t have dreamed of a better team to bring this wonderful universe to life.”

	Soumache, who is producing the film with Paul Trijbits via their company Magical Society,  said, “This film is not simply an adaptation, but a celebration of ‘The Little Prince,’ of its timeless story and its enduring spirit.” “Combining ‘The Little Prince,’ which has touched people young and old, with the adventurous, genius, passionate explorer and pilot Saint Exupéry is a magical mix,” he continued. 

	Trijbits, who runs Magical Society’s London office, previously executive produced Netflix family series “The Letter for the King” and Disney’s “Saving Mr. Banks,” along with films including Paul Greengrass’ “Bloody Sunday,” Andrea Arnold’s “Fish Tank” and Cary Fukunaga’s “Jane Eyre.”

	Sophie Kopaczynski, CEO of Le Petit Prince Groupe, said the aim was to honor Saint-Exupéry’s legacy while creating a film with broad international appeal.

	“Through his extraordinary life and writings, Antoine de Saint-Exupéry gave us a deeply humanist vision of the world that continues to resonate across generations and cultures,” said Kopaczynski, who previously held a senior position at Studiocanal and worked on several family entertainment franchises. “Our ambition is to honor his remarkable legacy through a spectacular cinematic adventure infused with the poetry and magic of ‘The Little Prince.’”

schema.headline: ‘The Little Prince’ Live-Action Movie Set With ‘The Imitation Game’ Director Morten Tyldum and Simon Beaufoy (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Curry Barker’s ‘Obsession’ Follow-Up ‘Anything But Ghosts’ Sets May 2027 Release Date From Focus Features, Blumhouse
description: Focus Features and Blumhouse-Atomic Monster have slated Curry Barker‘s upcoming horror-comedy “Anything But Ghosts” for release on May 7, 2027. Focu
body:
Focus Features and Blumhouse-Atomic Monster have slated Curry Barker‘s upcoming horror-comedy “Anything But Ghosts” for release on May 7, 2027. Focus has worldwide rights for the film, while Universal Pictures International will handle international distribution.

	Barker directs “Anything But Ghosts” and co-wrote the script with his “Obsession” star and longtime collaborator Cooper Tomlinson. The pair are also co-leads in the project, starring alongside Violet McGraw, Chris Reinacher, Bryce Dallas Howard and Aaron Paul.
	


	The official logline for the film reads, “When a group of fame-seeking wannabe ‘ghosthunters’ find themselves in over their heads, things spiral wildly and terrifyingly out of control.” 


	Roy Lee, Steven Schneider, Jason Blum, Adam Hendricks and Greg Gilreath serve as producers. Executive producers include Daniel Bekerman, Barker, Tomlinson and Ben Ross. Blumhouse-Atomic Monster, Spooky Pictures, Divide/Conquer produce in association with Image Nation and That’s a Bad Idea.

	Barker’s debut film “Obsession” was one of the biggest box office stories of the summer. The supernatural horror galvanized the Gen Z movie-going population and grossed $519 million worldwide against a budget of less than $1 million. It also achieved a 39% jump in earnings in its second weekend, a feat rarely seen in the current box office climate. 

	“Obsession” was also a critical smash, earning early Oscar buzz for Inde Navarrette, who co-starred in the project alongside Michael Johnston, Megan Lawless and Tomlinson. The film follows a hopelessly lonely young man named Bear (Johnston), who uses a mysterious toy called a “One Wish Willow” to make his crush, Nikki (Navarrette), fall for him. The wish, of course, goes terribly wrong, leading to bloody consequences for Bear, Nikki and their friends.

schema.headline: Curry Barker’s ‘Obsession’ Follow-Up ‘Anything But Ghosts’ Sets May 2027 Release Date From Focus Features, Blumhouse

title: Music Industry Moves: Universal Music Names Libby Bush President of Global Brands and Commercial Partnerships; Avex Acquires 85% of Brandon Silverstein’s S10 Entertainment
description: Universal Music Group has named Libby Bush to the newly created role of President, Global Brands and Commercial Partnerships, starting in November.
body:
Universal Music Group has named Libby Bush to the newly created role of President, Global Brands and Commercial Partnerships, starting in November. According to the announcement, she will “lead a new global function that brings together UMG’s brands, media, and commercial partnership businesses, including Universal Music Group for Brands … Spanning digital platforms, physical products and live experiences, these collaborations will be rooted in artists’ originality and authentic connections with fans.” Based in Los Angeles, Bush will report to UMG’s Chief Operating Officer Boyd Muir.
	

	She joins from Creative Artists Agency, where she served as Global Head of Entertainment Partnerships and was a member of the Agency Board. Previously, Bush founded Tandem Entertainment, an entertainment partnerships agency acquired by CAA in 2020, and held roles at Marvel Entertainment, ABC Entertainment, the WNBA’s Los Angeles Sparks and the National Basketball Association.


	Muir said, “As the ways fans experience music evolve, the opportunities for our artists multiply. Bringing our brand, media, and commercial partnerships together under Libby’s leadership will help extend our artists’ reach and grow their revenues, while giving our partners new ways to build relationships with fans and collaborate with the world’s most influential voices. Libby brings exceptional creative and commercial expertise to the world’s leading music company. She’ll work with our talent, teams, and partners to create memorable experiences for fans, lasting value for brands, and new possibilities for artists.”
	

	+ Avex Inc. has increased its ownership of Brandon Silverstein’s S10 Entertainment, acquiring 85% of the company from Silverstein and his partners. The transaction further integrates S10 into Avex Music Group. Silverstein continues as CEO of S10 and Avex Music Group, a board member and equity partner in Avex Music Group. Terms of the deal were not disclosed.

	The transaction follows Avex’s March 2025 acquisition of the S10 Music Publishing catalog, which includes shares of hits by Justin Bieber, Drake, Tate McRae, Kehlani, Doja Cat, Post Malone and Rihanna, among others. In the transaction Silverstein was represented by Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom LLP.

	“S10 is an exceptional management company that is playing a key role in realizing our global ambitions,” said Katsumi Kuroiwa, CEO of Avex Inc. “Bringing S10 into Avex reflects our confidence in Brandon’s leadership and our commitment to growing Avex’s global music business. Together, we will bring the full breadth of Avex’s capabilities to artists and creators around the world.”

	+ Warner Music Group has named Sonny Takhar as Chairman and CEO of Warner Music U.K. & Ireland, effective January 2027. Takhar will oversee creative direction, artist development, and strategic operations across WMG’s recorded music footprint in the U.K., the world’s third-largest music market, and Ireland.

	Takhar will report to Val Blavatnik, Managing Director of Warner Music North America, U.K. & Corporate Development. Takhar’s remit will also include operational oversight of WMG’s independent distribution arm, ADA, in the U.K. and Ireland, and he’ll work in close partnership with Elliot Grainge, CEO and Chairman of Atlantic Music Group and Chairman of ADA in the U.S., as well as Aaron Bay-Schuck, Chairman and CEO of Warner Records Group.

	A founding partner of Syco Entertainment, Takhar played a key role in the careers of One Direction, Labrinth, Leona Lewis, Little Mix, James Arthur and Fifth Harmony, alongside the launch of global TV franchises “The X Factor” and “Got Talent.” More recently, Takhar co-founded Los Angeles-based KYN Entertainment in a joint venture with Live Nation, and worked with Westlife and songwriter-producer Steve Mac.

	Blavatnik said, “Sonny is one of the most visionary executives in music and his track record of discovering, nurturing, and breaking global superstars speaks for itself. His instinct for talent, deep understanding of the wider music ecosystem and strategic global perspective make him the perfect leader to power Warner Music UK & Ireland forward.”
	

	+ Amra, the global digital collection society, today announced that its Chief Executive Officer, Tomas Ericsson, will transition from his role as CEO after 13 years, effective January 1, 2027. He will assume the role of Chairman of the Board. Robin Davies, Amra’s Chief Operating Officer for the last four years, has been named Chief Executive Officer of the company beginning on January 1st.

	Ericsson launched Amra in partnership with Kobalt Music Group in 2013, ultimately licensing digital rights directly across more than 200 territories, 45 publishers and growing into nine figures gross by 2026.

	“We are so grateful for Tomas’ vision and leadership as he and his team have built amra into one of the industry’s most innovative and transformational organizations,” said Laurent Hubert, CEO of Kobalt. “We are also looking forward to Tomas continuing to contribute to the business as Chairman. amra will be in good hands with Tomas’ ongoing guidance and with Robin, who has been with amra and the Kobalt organization for a decade, at the helm.”

	+ Danny Goldberg has promoted Jesse Bauer to the position of Senior Vice-President and Gabriel Barreto to Vice President of Gold Village Entertainment, the New York based artist management company that Goldberg launched in 2007. Bauer has been with the company since its inception; Barreto joined in 2021. Gold Village represents Steve Earle, the Waterboys, and others.

	+ Music Services, a division of SESAC Music Group, has named Nick LaPointe Senior Director of Business Development, and Jay Sudarma Vice President of Marketing for Music Services and CCLI Group. LaPointe joins from FUGA AVS and previously held roles at AdRev and Warner Chappell Music; Sudarm’s new role comes alongside a promotion to Vice President of Marketing at CCLI Group, where he previously served as Director of Marketing. Both appointments are effective immediately.

	“We’re thrilled to welcome Nick to the team. Throughout his career, he has earned the trust of independent publishers and labels by helping them turn their rights into meaningful revenue,” said Rose Cook, Chief Operating Officer, Music Services. “During his tenure at CCLI, Jay has proven the value of a disciplined, data-driven approach to marketing, and this expanded role is a natural next step,” said Cook. “He will work across brands in the Music Services portfolio, including AudioSalad, Audiam, Music Services Inc., The Harry Fox Agency, HAAWK, and CCLI, bringing a unified voice to a growing collection of brands while preserving the qualities that make each one unique.”
	

	+ ASCAP President and Chairman of the Board Paul Williams has announced that Jim Selby has been elected as a publisher member to the ASCAP Board of Directors. Jim Selby is President, Global Music Publishing at BMG, leading the company’s worldwide music publishing, and played a key role in its recent merger with Concord.

	Williams commented: “The ASCAP Board cares deeply about making decisions that are in the best interests of the membership as a whole. As a global publishing leader, Jim has the expertise to tackle the complex issues facing music creators and publishers in today’s market, from both the challenges and opportunities of AI to licensees who want to pay songwriters less. He will be an invaluable voice on the ASCAP Board in our mission to advocate for and protect our more than one million members.”

	+ Universal Music Group has named Òscar Celma as Senior Vice President, Applied AI and Machine Learning, effective immediately. Celma will help lead the development and application of AI and machine learning across UMG’s global operations, supporting UMG’s labels, divisions and businesses. He will report to Hannah Poferl, UMG’s Chief Data Officer.

	In his previous role at Spotify, Celma helped lead the development of AI-powered personalized listening experiences including AI DJ, Jam and Daylist, as well as personalization and discovery. He also held roles at Conde Nast, Pandora/SiriusXM and BMAT Music Innovators.

	Poferl said, “Òscar brings a unique blend of quantitative and product experience, deep expertise in AI, and a love of music. He’s built teams that have delivered and knows how to turn data at scale into useful insights. With the breadth and depth of UMG’s data, there’s enormous potential for him to help our teams do more for our artists.”

	+ Chrysalis Records, part of the Reservoir group of companies, and associated artist management & music publishing company Blue Raincoat Music announced that broadcaster-journalist Steve Lamacq has joined the company as Curator, New Music & Talent Development. The newly created consultancy role focused on helping both companies identify, champion and nurture the next generation of breakthrough artists.

	Working alongside Chrysalis’ and Blue Raincoat’s existing A&R, management and creative teams in a consultancy capacity, Lamacq, a veteran of the BBC and NME, will help discover, champion and develop emerging talent, drawing on more than four decades of experience at the forefront of alternative and independent music culture. Lamacq was appointed an MBE in 2025 for services to broadcasting and to music venues.
	

	Jeremy Lascelles, CEO of Chrysalis Records & Blue Raincoat Music said: “Steve has an extraordinary ability to spot great artists early. Time and again he’s identified talent long before the wider industry catches on. When I asked him if he fancied working alongside us in this capacity, I was over the proverbial moon when he agreed. It’s pretty much a dream scenario for us. Alongside his deep knowledge of music, he has built a level of trust with artists and audiences alike, that makes him uniquely qualified for this curating role. I’m thrilled with the association and think we’re going to have a lot of fun.”

title: Chris Brown’s $13 Million Jury Award to Ex-Housekeeper Could Be Slashed By Judge
description:

                          Judge Looks to Slash $13 Million Award To Ex-Housekeeper Ov
body:
Chris Brown
                          Judge Looks to Slash $13 Million Award To Ex-Housekeeper Over Dog Attack
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 29, 2026
                            1:11 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Chris Brown scored a huge victory in his legal battle with his ex-housekeeper over a vicious dog attack … with the judge giving him a new trial on damages if she doesn't agree to reduce her award by millions ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            According to court docs, obtained by TMZ, a Los Angeles County Superior Court judge granted the singer's request for a new trial on damages in the case brought by Maria Avila … but only if Maria doesn't sign off on her award being reduced from $12.9 million to $9.5 million. 
      
    
            The judge found there was "insufficient evidence of permanent nerve damage and of the value assigned to future pain and suffering" in reaching the ruling that the jury's award to Avila was excessive.
      
    
            As we previously reported, Maria claimed she was working at Chris' Tarzana home in 2020 when a large dog attacked her while taking out the trash.
      
    
            Chris denied wrongdoing, but a jury ended up awarding her $12.9 million in damages after a trial where both parties took the stand to testify.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            As TMZ first reported, Chris argued he should have a new trial because the court allowed things like his past arrests, including his Rihanna incident, to be discussed in the trial.
      
    
            Maria has been seeking a cut of Chris' tour profits from his concerts with Usher to satisfy the massive judgment.

title: Mama June's Ex Sugar Bear Engaged to Woman He Met On TikTok
description:
Mama June's Ex Sugar Bear
                          I Found Love on TikTok!!!
body:
Mama June's Ex Sugar Bear
                          I Found Love on TikTok!!!
                          Engaged 5 Months Later
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 29, 2026
                            3:45 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Mama June's ex, Mike "Sugar Bear" Thompson, is engaged again ... and this time, he says he's found love on TikTok.
      
    
            Sugar Bear tells TMZ ... he proposed to his girlfriend, Taylor, Sunday during a TikTok Live at her home in Georgia ... giving her a ring that once belonged to her mom. SB tells us he asked Taylor's mom for her blessing before popping the question.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The couple met on TikTok about five months ago after Sugar Bear reached out to her first ... and they say their chemistry was immediate.
      

            Taylor says Sugar Bear initially came over to her house, where she made him "a big ol' pot of spaghetti." They spent the weekend together talking and having fun before their relationship blossomed.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The couple now live together, and Sugar Bear tells TMZ he's living his life and taking things one day at a time. 
      
    
            He says Taylor is "sweet and very pretty," while Taylor tells us she really likes him and says they started meeting up and hanging out before eventually moving in together.
      
    
            As for wedding plans ... the couple says they're taking their time and are thinking sometime next year, though they haven't decided on a location.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Sugar Bear was previously in a long-term relationship with Mama June ... and they met in an online chat room. They held a commitment ceremony in 2013 and share daughter Alana "Honey Boo Boo" Thompson, but they were never legally married. 
      
    
            They split in 2014, and Mike later married Jennifer Lamb in 2017.

title: Cornell Alleged Gang Rape: District Attorney Meeting With Accuser This Week
description:
Cornell Alleged Gang Rape
                          D.A. Meeting Accuser This Week
body:
Cornell Alleged Gang Rape
                          D.A. Meeting Accuser This Week
                          ... After Her Lawyer Slams Law Enforcement
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 29, 2026
                            1:42 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The alleged rape victim in the Cornell University scandal is set to meet with the District Attorney this week, TMZ has learned. 
      
    
            The Tompkins County D.A., Matthew Van Houten, revealed he is in communication with Jane Doe's lawyer about an interview. 
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Van Houten said he spoke to Doe's team about cooperating with the "grand jury process and what that looks like."
      

            He told People on Tuesday, "My hope is that we will connect with him and Jane Doe as early as tomorrow and start that process." 
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The move comes after Doe's lawyer slammed Cornell University officials for not taking action after the alleged victim went to police in 2024 ... shortly after the alleged incident. Law enforcement said they investigated the matter but did not believe a crime had occurred. 
      
    
            The criminal case was reopened after Doe filed a bombshell civil lawsuit this month, claiming she was gang raped by 7 fraternity brothers from Chi Phi. No criminal charges have been filed.
